answer: In a market where agents trade river water rights, saffron, and plots on a knoll, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked in escrow, with no bonus per account. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period and paying the opportunity cost of funds it cannot use elsewhere.
